answer: The place I would like to describe is a public park not far from where I live, which is a real green oasis in the middle of our town. It is only about ten minutes' walk from our flat, so it is very easy to reach. I try to visit at least once a week, usually on Friday afternoons, and more often in winter when the weather is pleasant. It is beautifully [[landscaped]], with wide lawns, tall shady trees and a small pond in the middle, surrounded by flower beds that are at their best in early spring. There is also a walking track around the edge and a little play area for children. Sirajganj is getting more built up every year, so having such a [[lush]] green space nearby is genuinely precious. I usually go there to walk, read or simply sit on a bench and [[watch the world go by]]. What I love most is how it brings the community together; families picnic, children play cricket on the grass and elderly men sit chatting for hours. The atmosphere is always [[laid-back]] and cheerful, and nobody seems to be in a hurry. Honestly, spending time surrounded by greenery has a noticeably [[restorative]] effect on me, especially after a stressful week at work. Sometimes I take my four-year-old nephew there when my elder sister visits from Dhaka, and watching him run around is a joy in itself. I think every town needs places like this, and I feel lucky to have one so close.

followUps.q: Do you think your town needs more parks?
followUps.answer: Yes, definitely. The town is growing quickly and new buildings are going up everywhere, so green spaces are shrinking. More parks would give children somewhere safe to play and give everyone a place to breathe.

followUps.q: What do you usually do there at the weekend?
followUps.answer: Mostly I walk a few laps of the track and then sit under a tree with a book. Sometimes I meet a friend there, and we buy roasted peanuts from a vendor and chat for an hour.

note: City changed to town (Sirajganj); duck lake made a pond; added layout, nephew visit; plain mark 'relaxed' replaced by 'laid-back', added 'watch the world go by'.
